239: It's written ״You shall not make molten gods for yourselves” (Shemot 34:17) and afterwards it is written ״You shall keep the feast of unleavened bread (Ibid 34:18).” What does this [verse] have to do with that one? Rather, this is the explanation: one who eats chametz on Pesach is similar to one who worships idols.

Come and see! When the Jewish people went out of Egypt, they went out from their domain; from the 'other' domain, from that domain which is called chametz, bad bread. And that is why the [worship of] stars and constellations is called this. And this is the secret of the evil impulse, foreign service, that is also called leaven. And that is the evil impulse. For the evil impulse is like this with people, like the leaven in the dough. It enters the innards of people little by little; and afterwards it grows in him, to the point that his whole body is mixed with it. And that is [the way of] the stars and constellations. And it is about this that it is written (Psalms 81:10), "There shall not be a strange god within you" - certainly a strange god.
